目前没有中文，考虑到文本量巨大，即使有人汉化也可能要时间 界面有点带复古风格的文字冒险，你会不断遇到各种事件以及做出选择来看影响和结果，有些会有扔骰子检定。有些属于一连串事件，触发A事件之后，后续会有接着的B事件。还有些可能影响到结局。不少事件还是比较有意思的，而且很多事件本身也会有三四个甚至更多的选项可以选，能看到很多发展分支 一般流程分成两个阶段，第一阶段通过选择来确定颜色、特性、形态等基础数据，再过几次培养事件之后成形确定蘑菇的种类。第二阶段你将扮演蘑菇娘，开始一段冒险，经历四个季节到达结局 现在做了评分系统，会有花园等功能来改变你下一次培养蘑菇时，她成长的倾向，后面还会解锁加速成长从而快速跳过第一个阶段 游戏里最核心的就是一个个短篇故事，其实有点像看聊斋志异一样。世界观接近于经典的魔法与剑中世纪题材，当然也有一些比较天马行空的事件。总体而言都是蘑菇娘作为主角参与的事件，选项方面也给了一些神奇展开的选择，所以比较有意思 游戏也做了很多蘑菇娘种类，并且做了很多对应的蘑菇娘立绘以及人设，都是有现实蘑菇原型的，一些小细节也做得不赖，有几个蘑菇娘应该是有专属事件或者专属分支啥的，不过包括demo以及现在正式版玩到的总共十多种蘑菇娘来看，就算有可能也不多，也许也是考虑到第二阶段的事件总数不算特别多然后没有怎么做吧，略微可惜

A survivalist shut-in learns that there are single witches in his area and thus clicks the link to find out more on how they can net him a daughter. Three trifling tasks and a visit to Gnome Depot later and you're playing as the titular title drop in a coffee break game with many, many mushroom mademoiselles and also a pocket potato princess for some reason. And whether your Portabello goes off to slay Moby Pork, your Cordyceps conquers the classroom, or your Fairy Ring joins the Unseelie Court in their tooth fairy tooth racketeering racket is up to the choices you make over the next three seasons of this game and it's technicolor dreamcoat. Seriously I've never seen so many color schemes in a game. That alone, while not worth the price of admission, is close to about maybe a third of the ticket to this three-ring Brothers Grimm-looking mycological [i]Princess Maker[/i] circus. 8/10, Aspergillus and Penicillium still need to be refined and processed in order to be usable as the levels of mycotoxin present in their unrefined state are generally unsafe for human consumption on top of being carcinogenic. Mithridatism, while a real practice, is not a guarantee that one can safely consume that moldy bread in your pantry that you've been meaning to throw out for the past three months. Yes, your pantry.

Full disclosure, I originally got this through illegitimate means. After liking the game enough, I decided to buy it. The review is missing a generous number of hours as a result. I'm still thankful to the developers for their patience as I tried to transfer my progress. I'd actually suggest checking out the demo though because of the type of content it has The game is an incredibly accessible choose-your-own-adventure visual novel made using Renpy with a ridiculous amount of factors and branching paths that make each run fun, and it has a lot of really good accessibility features to be approachable including speech-to-text that are personally very useful. The game is still largely a VN, but it has equal parts gardening simulator and virtual pet, at least early on. How you handle things also will affect how future runs work in a way that means you actually DO only get better as you continue, and if you need to play worse for some of those stubborn achievements? That's doable, too. The daughters you can raise are all cute and the game's writing does factor in how many and who you raised, and what role they take around your playthroughs... for example, I had one mushroom daughter become the Dude, and now every time I see the Dude, it's just that daughter. Stuff like that makes this really easily enjoyable. Combined with the frequency of the auto saves and how quick it is to dump out a run in general, this is a perfect game for short breaks, or if it ever ends up mobile, even going on the go.

I played the demo for this game and was immediately enchanted. From the unique blend of spritework and pixelated photographs to the tranquil music and tight writing, my first experience of Mushroom Musume was that it was a charming visual novel, with both heart and intrigue aplenty. Immediately wishlisted it and bought it when it came out a week later. Unfortunately, after playing a few more runs, I realized something: the game is very, very, repetitive. I went in knowing that some degree of seeing the same scenarios again and again would be unavoidable; just mathematically, its impossible to have completely unique runs over time with the number of events points each one has. That being said, I was shocked by how immediately the tedium started to set in. It's caught between wanting to be both a roguelike and a narrative visual novel, and ends up sacrificing the strength of the latter for the sake of the former.

Ever wondered what it would be like to have a fungal daughter? Ever wondered what life would be like as such a creature? Well, this game seems the closest thing we'll ever get to unravelling this mycelian mystery. Unfortunately I do not recommend it. While the game oozes charm the core gameplay experience is lacking. The game is heavily progression based. You'll have random events where your chance of succeeding is aided by your stats. Your stats seem to mostly come from the witch's garden, which is slowly improved for each completed playthrough. This means success is a given... well, given time. Once you understand this you realize that the best course of action is to just grind playthroughs until your garden is full of funny little mushrooms and your daughter's starting stats become impressive. At that point, you'll have a greater ability to actually navigate your way through the game's events. With that said, everything else is lovely. It's almost as if the game's content would have been better served as a quirky visual novel.

I love my mushroom daughters. If you like games like Princess Maker, Volcano Princess, or Long Live The Queen - stuff like that - you will thoroughly enjoy this game. The sessions, once you have played a couple rounds to utilize the skip function, can be fairly short making it for a nice not commital thing for when you want to game but maybe only habe 30-60 minutes. Obviously to make it that fast you will have needed to have done a couple rounds but from there it gets faster like trying to find a different route in your typical visual novel after playing your first couple routes. You skip the repeating parts and enjoy what is new. And as you play at the end of each session you get spores which you can use to unlock new mushroom girl types or even get temporary items to make your next playthrough go in a specific direction stat-wise and so on. There is a lot to love about this game. A run is definitely shorter than Princess Maker, Volcano Princess, or Long Live The Queen but the replayability is endless. Full recommend even at full price. Mushroom Musume was a joy to play from start to finish, even after many hours of dozens of runs, I was still excited to discover new scenarios and endings up to the very end. I cannot praise the writing enough, being a perfect blend of horror, wit, and slice-of-life, making every new scene and choice worth reading, combined with a consistently stunning soundtrack, beautifully photographed backgrounds, and even light RPG mechanics. The overarching story gradually unfolding over the course of your many daughters’ lives is done incredibly well, going to unbelievable lengths and culminating in something truly spectacular. Even outside of the “main” story, everything comes together in a way that makes the world feel truly large and lived in – plenty of persistent changes and progression, unique lines of dialogue acknowledging other events or your daughter’s unique traits, and a wide range of distinct and charming NPCs that often play much larger roles than you’d think. It’s a joy to get lost in Mushroom Musume’s world and I only came to love the game more as I played, seeing the fascinating places the story would go and running into an endless amount of charming and witty scenarios. It can be difficult to truly discover everything with the limited amount of time in each run coupled with the large pool of events, but thankfully quick saving and loading is painless and can be used to reroll and obtain any outcome you want. There is also a very helpful miraheze wiki for the game when needed, but I will say that paying attention to the game will also often put you on the right path, giving you context clues to investigate on your next run, or perhaps on a daughter with a specific trait. I also feel that the deceptively huge number of things to discover in this game is one of its biggest strengths and means I’m rarely just doing a run for the sake of it, there’s always something I wanted to check out or progress, or I’d stumble upon something new anyway! It may not seem like there’s much at the start, but I highly recommend sticking with Mushroom Musume and seeing where the world takes you, I really believe it’s something special and I can tell a huge amount of love and passion was poured into this amazingly adorable little game. And as a lesbian, yes, the abundance of women and wlw relationships being the norm is so refreshing.

Simple indie game, growing a mushroom daughter. Been playing since august 2025 demo till full release more recent months. It's fun little game if your into complex story's. I always love finding the outcome of each of them. Even the mini story's within the game, a perspective how this all came to be. With all the different witches and times to make essentially what becomes "You"! It has been very calming to me especially if i want to past some time in classes. Or when I'm frustrated and need to calm down with something. The stories progress each time you go through the game, if its doing something different, or changing yourself to become better. It is hard however getting something different. You have to look deep into the game. All the daughters are unique to their personality's as well. Tending your mushroom garden also takes a big effect how the daughter behaves or turns out to be. The better you take care of the garden the better you have chances of getting something different in a certain field, i always make sure my girls are close to 100 of everything as possible if not i work up. sometimes certain traits could kill them, you don't wanna get to 0. Death is a possibility as well in this game, if its saving someone or killing someone. always a risk to your own consequences. It does has a bit of a D&D element to them so most events are almost completely random. i love a good game of chance. My favorite route is when you go out on a date with the thief towards the end of the run to steal things. if successful you can just chill up on the roof into the stars. The only complaint might just be a bug or steam issue but none of my achievement i got sync onto steam achievements which sucks because i really enjoy this game and just look like I've just ran it for all those hours instead of trying to get them. but in game i have A lot of them hopefully this gets fixed.
